_comment: List of all daily-use flags and combinations for every real-world workflow pattern people actually run into

commands.name: git init
common_forms_and_flags: git init — create repo in current directory (local)
common_workflows: mkdir proj && cd proj && git init — start local project
git init --bare /srv/git/repo.git — create server repo
After init: create .gitignore, git add ., git commit -m "initial"
commands.notes: --bare repos have no working tree; used for remotes.

commands.name: git clone
common_forms_and_flags: git clone --single-branch — only fetch specified branch
git clone --mirror <url> — mirror clone for bare backup
git clone --config core.autocrlf=true <url> — set config on clone
GIT_SSH_COMMAND='ssh -i key' git clone <url> — custom ssh key
common_workflows: git clone -b develop --single-branch git@host:org/repo.git — clone only develop
git clone --depth 1 <url> — quick shallow copy for CI
Clone then git checkout -b myfeature origin/main or git switch -c
commands.notes: --depth reduces history; to fetch more history later: git fetch --unshallow or git fetch --depth=<n>.

commands.name: git add
common_forms_and_flags: git add . — stage all changed (in pwd)
git add -A — stage all changes (including deletions)
git add -u — stage tracked changes and deletions (no new files)
git add -p — interactive patch add (very common)
git add --intent-to-add <file> — record intent-to-add (index entry with no content)
common_workflows: git add -p → selectively stage hunks before git commit
git add -A && git commit -m "..." — stage everything
git add <file> && git restore --staged <file> — stage then unstage
commands.notes: Use git status --porcelain to see staged vs unstaged.

commands.name: git mv
common_workflows: git mv file1.js dir/ && git commit -m "move file1 to dir"
If moving without git mv: mv old new && git add new && git rm old
commands.notes: git mv is convenience: it stages move and removal.

commands.name: git restore
common_forms_and_flags: git restore <file> — restore file from HEAD (discard working tree changes)
git restore --staged <file> — unstage file (move from index to working tree)
git restore --source <ref> -- <path> — restore from given commit/ref
git restore --worktree --staged <file> — restore both index and working tree (rare)
common_workflows: git restore --staged file — move staged change back to unstaged
git restore --source origin/main -- file — undo local edits to match remote branch
commands.notes: git restore replaces older patterns (git checkout -- file).

commands.name: git rm
common_forms_and_flags: git rm <file> — remove from index and working tree
git rm --cached <file> — remove from index but keep file (stop tracking)
common_workflows: git rm --cached file && echo file >> .gitignore && git add .gitignore && git commit -m "stop tracking file"
git rm -r build/ && git commit -m "remove build artifacts"
commands.notes: --cached useful for removing secrets from tracking but leaving local copy.

commands.name: git commit
common_forms_and_flags: git commit — opens editor for message
git commit -a -m "msg" — auto-stage tracked changes (does not add new files)
git commit --amend — amend last commit (change message or contents)
git commit -v — verbose (shows diff in editor)
common_workflows: git add -p && git commit -m "fix: ..." — selective staging + commit
git commit --amend --no-edit — add staged changes to previous commit without editing message
git commit --amend -m "new message" && git push --force-with-lease — change message already pushed (force-push needed)
git commit -a -m "..." && git push — common quick flow
commands.notes: Amending and then force-pushing is common but requires care with shared branches (--force-with-lease safer).

commands.name: git status
common_forms_and_flags: git status --porcelain=2 — parseable output for scripts
common_workflows: git status before add/commit to see changes
git status -sb — shows branch and short status
commands.notes: Use porcelain output in GUIs and scripts.

commands.name: git diff
common_forms_and_flags: git diff — unstaged changes vs working tree
git diff --staged or --cached — changes staged for commit
git diff <commit> — differences between working tree and commit
git diff <commit1> <commit2> or git diff <ref>..<ref> — commit-to-commit diffs
git diff --no-index — diff files not in repo
common_workflows: git diff -> fix -> git add -p -> git commit
git diff origin/main..HEAD — show your changes compared to remote main
Use git diff --staged to verify staged content before git commit
commands.notes: Good for generating patches: git diff > my.patch or git format-patch.

commands.name: git log
common_forms_and_flags: git log --oneline — compact single-line per commit
git log --graph --decorate --oneline — visual branch graph (very common)
git log --since="2 weeks ago" / --until — time filtering
git log -p — patch per commit (show diffs)
git log --name-only — file list per commit
git log <branch1>..<branch2> — commits in branch2 but not branch1
common_workflows: git log --graph --decorate --oneline --all — visualize all branches
git log origin/main..HEAD --oneline — local commits not pushed
commands.notes: --oneline is widely used in UIs and CLI.

commands.name: git show
common_forms_and_flags: git show <commit>:path/to/file — view file at commit
common_workflows: git show HEAD~2 — inspect earlier commit
git show origin/main:README.md — view remote file
commands.notes: git show can inspect blobs/trees directly.

commands.name: git branch
common_forms_and_flags: git branch -d <name> — delete branch (safe: refuses unmerged)
git branch --contains <commit> — branches that contain commit
common_workflows: git branch -b? (use git checkout -b or git switch -c instead)
git branch -d feature — delete merged branch
After push: git push origin --delete feature to remove remote
commands.notes: -d safety prevents data loss.

commands.name: git checkout
common_forms_and_flags: git checkout -b <new> — create + switch (legacy; prefer git switch -c)
git checkout -- <file> — restore file from HEAD (legacy)
git checkout <commit> -- <file> — get file version from commit
git checkout --detach <commit> — check out a commit in detached HEAD
common_workflows: git checkout -b myfeature origin/main — create branch from remote
git checkout -- file — discard local edits to file
commands.notes: Prefer git switch and git restore for clarity.

commands.name: git switch
common_forms_and_flags: git switch --discard-changes <branch> — (older flags) usually --force to discard
common_workflows: git switch -c myfeature — start feature
git switch main && git pull — update main
commands.notes: switch is clearer than checkout for branch switching.

commands.name: git merge
common_forms_and_flags: git merge <branch> — merge branch into current
git merge --no-ff <branch> — create merge commit even if fast-forward
git merge --squash <branch> — prepare squashed changes without commit
git merge --abort — abort during conflict resolution
git merge --no-commit — don’t auto-commit merge result
common_workflows: git checkout main && git merge --no-ff feature-x — explicit merge commit
git merge --squash feature && git commit -m "squashed changes" — squash merge locally
git pull may run merge as part of fetch + merge
commands.notes: When conflicts: edit files, git add resolved files, then git commit (or git merge --continue depending on state).

commands.name: git rebase
common_forms_and_flags: git rebase <base> — reapply commits on top of <base>
git rebase -i <base> — interactive rebase (squash, fixup, reword)
git pull --rebase — fetch & rebase local commits onto updated upstream
git rebase -x "cmd" — run command after each commit (advanced)
common_workflows: git checkout feature && git rebase -i origin/main — clean up commits before merge/push
git pull --rebase origin main — keep linear local history
commands.notes: Rewriting shared history requires force-push afterward: git push --force-with-lease.

commands.name: git cherry-pick
common_forms_and_flags: git cherry-pick <commit> — apply commit to current branch
git cherry-pick -x <commit> — add (cherry picked from ...) note (very common)
common_workflows: git cherry-pick -x abc123 — bring bugfix commit to release branch, keeping reference
git cherry-pick -n commit1 commit2 && git commit -m "combined" — combine picks into single commit
commands.notes: Use -x for traceability.

commands.name: git revert
common_forms_and_flags: git revert <commit> — create new commit that undoes <commit>
git revert --no-edit — use default message and auto-commit
git revert -n — revert without committing (batch reverts)
git revert --mainline <parent-number> — revert a merge commit
common_workflows: git revert -m 1 <merge-commit> — undo a bad merge (mainline selection)
git revert <commit> && git push — safe undo on shared branch
commands.notes: revert is the safe way to undo a commit already published.

commands.name: git tag
common_forms_and_flags: git tag -a v1.0 -m "release v1.0" — annotated tag (recommended)
git tag v1.0 <commit> — tag specific commit
git tag -d v1.0 and git push origin :refs/tags/v1.0 — delete local + remote tag
common_workflows: git tag -a v1.2.3 -m "release notes" && git push origin v1.2.3
Lightweight tag: git tag v1.2.3
commands.notes: Use annotated tags for releases (include message, signing -s available).

commands.name: git fetch
common_forms_and_flags: git fetch — fetch all remotes configured
git fetch origin — fetch from origin
git fetch --prune — remove tracking refs that no longer exist on remote
git fetch origin <branch> — fetch specific ref
common_workflows: git fetch origin && git log ..origin/main — inspect remote changes before merge
git fetch --prune — clean stale remote branches
commands.notes: fetch only updates local remote-tracking branches; you must merge/rebase/checkout to incorporate.

commands.name: git pull
common_forms_and_flags: git pull --rebase — fetch + rebase local commits
git pull origin main — specify remote/branch
common_workflows: git pull --rebase origin main — common to avoid merge commits
Use git fetch + examine before git merge for safer updates
commands.notes: pull is a convenience that can cause unexpected merges; many prefer fetch + manual merge/rebase.

commands.name: git push
common_forms_and_flags: git push — push current branch to default remote
git push origin main — push specific branch
git push --set-upstream origin feature or -u — set upstream
git push origin :branch or git push --delete origin branch — delete remote branch
common_workflows: git push -u origin feature — first push to set upstream
After rebase or commit --amend: git push --force-with-lease
CI gating: git push triggers pipelines
commands.notes: Prefer --force-with-lease over --force when rewriting history.

commands.name: git remote
common_forms_and_flags: git remote add origin <url> — add remote
git remote remove <name> or git remote rm <name>
git remote show origin — show verbose info
common_workflows: git remote add origin git@host:org/repo.git && git push -u origin main
git remote set-url origin git@newhost:org/repo.git — change remote
commands.notes: Use git remote -v to see fetch/push URL.

commands.name: git ls-remote
common_forms_and_flags: git ls-remote <url> — list refs on remote
common_workflows: Check remote refs before cloning or pushing (useful in scripts)

commands.name: git credential
common_forms_and_flags: git credential fill, git credential approve, git credential reject — used by helpers
git config --global credential.helper store — save credentials
common_workflows: Configure credential helpers: git config --global credential.helper cache or store or manager-core (platform dependent)
commands.notes: Use OS credential managers (manager-core) for secure storage.

commands.name: git stash (group)
common_forms_and_flags: git stash push or git stash — stash changes
git stash push --include-untracked or -u — include untracked files
git stash push --all or -a — include ignored files too
git stash show — show last stash summary
git stash apply [<stash>] — apply stash without dropping
git stash pop [<stash>] — apply and drop (commonly git stash pop)
git stash branch <branch> [<stash>] — create branch from stash
common_workflows: git stash push -u — keep working directory clean to switch branch
git stash pop — apply stash and drop (common)
git stash branch myfix stash@{0} — create branch from stash for separate work
commands.notes: Stashes are numbered stash@{0}; use git stash show -p stash@{1} to view patch.

commands.name: git apply
common_forms_and_flags: git apply patch.diff — apply patch to working tree
git apply --index patch.diff — apply patch and update index (stage)
git apply --check patch.diff — check if patch applies
common_workflows: git format-patch -> email -> git am to apply series as commits
wget example.patch && git apply --index example.patch && git commit -m "apply patch"
commands.notes: git apply will not create commits unless used with index + commit.

commands.name: git bisect
common_forms_and_flags: git bisect bad — mark current as bad
git bisect good <commit> — mark known good
git bisect run <test-script> — automate bisection with script exit codes
common_workflows: git bisect start -> git bisect bad -> git bisect good v1.2 -> git bisect run ./test.sh — find bad commit via tests
commands.notes: Bisection requires deterministic tests.

commands.name: git grep
common_workflows: git grep -n "TODO" origin/main..HEAD — search changes in range
Use in scripts: git grep -l pattern | xargs ...

commands.name: git blame
common_forms_and_flags: git blame <file> — annotate lines with commit/author
common_workflows: git blame -L 1,200 README.md — find who last changed a section

commands.name: git clean
common_forms_and_flags: git clean -f — force delete untracked files
git clean -fdx — delete ignored files too (dangerous)
common_workflows: git clean -fdn then git clean -fd — ensure safe removal
commands.notes: Use with caution; -x deletes ignored files including config.

commands.name: git archive
common_workflows: git archive --format=tar --output=release.tar HEAD — export snapshot for release

commands.name: git bundle
common_forms_and_flags: git bundle create repo.bundle --all — create bundle file
git clone repo.bundle <dir> — clone from bundle
git bundle verify repo.bundle — check integrity
git bundle list-heads repo.bundle — list refs inside bundle
common_workflows: Transfer repository without network: create bundle, copy, and clone/apply.

commands.name: git submodule
common_forms_and_flags: git submodule init — initialize local config
git submodule update — fetch checked-out commit
git submodule update --init --recursive — init + update recursively
git submodule foreach 'git pull origin main' — operate across submodules
common_workflows: git clone --recurse-submodules — clone including submodules
git submodule add git@host:lib.git vendor/lib — add external dependency
commands.notes: Submodules are a common source of confusion; using --recurse-submodules reduces surprises.

commands.name: git worktree
common_forms_and_flags: git worktree add <path> <branch> — create working tree for branch
git worktree prune — prune stale worktrees
common_workflows: git worktree add ../w-tree feature-branch — work on multiple branches concurrently
commands.notes: Worktrees share the same object database but separate working trees.

commands.name: git config
common_forms_and_flags: git config user.name "Name" / git config user.email "a@b"
common_workflows: git config --global credential.helper store
git config pull.rebase true — default pull to rebase
commands.notes: Configs can be set per-repo or global.

commands.name: git help
common_workflows: git help commit — read docs on commit usage

commands.name: git describe
common_forms_and_flags: git describe --tags — describe commit by nearest tag
git describe --always — show commit hash if no tag
git describe --dirty — append -dirty if working tree changed
common_workflows: Use git describe --tags --long to generate human-friendly build versions.

commands.name: git daemon
common_workflows: git daemon can serve repositories via the git protocol for anonymous read access (rare; used for quick sharing)
commands.notes: Usually replaced by SSH/HTTP(S) hosting; do not expose without security considerations.

commands.name: git reset
common_forms_and_flags: git reset --soft <commit> — move HEAD, keep staged & working tree (keeps changes staged)
git reset --mixed <commit> (default) — move HEAD, keep working tree, unstage changes
git reset --hard <commit> — move HEAD and reset index & working tree (destructive)
git reset <file> — unstage file (legacy; git restore --staged preferred)
common_workflows: git reset --soft HEAD~1 — uncommit but keep changes staged
git reset --hard origin/main — make branch exactly match remote (dangerous)
commands.notes: --hard will delete uncommitted changes.

commands.name: git reflog
common_forms_and_flags: git reflog — show reference log for HEAD
common_workflows: After accidental reset --hard, use git reflog to find previous HEAD then git checkout -b recover <sha>.
commands.notes: git reflog used to recover lost commits: git checkout <sha> from reflog.

commands.name: git filter-branch / git filter-repo
common_forms_and_flags: git filter-repo --path filename --invert-paths (modern, external tool; much faster & safer)
common_workflows: Rewriting history to remove secrets: prefer git filter-repo and then force-push (git push --force-with-lease)
commands.notes: History rewriting is destructive—coordinate with collaborators.

commands.name: git cherry
common_forms_and_flags: git cherry -v <upstream> <head> — find commits unique to head (not merged)
common_workflows: Evaluate which commits are not merged to upstream.

commands.name: git format-patch
common_forms_and_flags: git format-patch origin/main — create patches for commits on current branch not in origin/main
git format-patch --stdout — output patches to stdout
common_workflows: git format-patch -3 → send patches via email or apply with git am

commands.name: git am
common_forms_and_flags: git am <patches> — apply mailbox patches as commits
git am --3way — attempt 3-way merge on conflicts
common_workflows: Receiving emailed patches: git am 0001-some-fix.patch

commands.name: git rerere
common_forms_and_flags: git config --global rerere.enabled true — enable reuse recorded resolutions
git rerere status, git rerere clear — auxiliary commands
common_workflows: Helpful when repeatedly rebasing/merging the same conflicts.
commands.notes: git rerere commands are mostly automatic.

commands.name: git shortlog
common_forms_and_flags: git shortlog -s -n origin/main..HEAD — contributions summary by author
common_workflows: Prepare CONTRIBUTORS or release notes.

commands.name: git fsck
common_workflows: Run on server/backup to verify repo health.

commands.name: git verify-pack
common_workflows: Diagnose pack bloat & check sizes prior to prune/gc.

commands.name: git count-objects
common_forms_and_flags: git count-objects -v — verbose repo object summary
common_workflows: Quick repo size diagnostics.

commands.name: git prune
common_forms_and_flags: git prune --expire <time> — expire older than given time
common_workflows: Run before git gc for cleanup.
commands.notes: Dangerous on backups; ensure you have refs.

commands.name: git gc
common_workflows: Scheduled server maintenance: git gc --aggressive occasionally.

commands.name: git whatchanged
common_workflows: Replaced by git log --name-status --pretty=...
